Key Takeaways

Palo Alto Networks shares rose 3% today after Deutsche Bank named it one of three standouts among companies set to gain from rising AI usage, while the Nasdaq fell about 2%.

CEO Nikesh Arora warned that more AI-found flaws like this week's PHP bug are coming, and Cloudflare rose [4%] as the cybersecurity rally carried on.

When AI finds flaws faster, companies have to spend more to defend against them, and that makes Palo Alto a hedge against AI's risks.

The stock already reflects a lot of that demand, with its forward P/E well above its five-year average.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW:NASDAQ) shares are up 3% today, while the Nasdaq is down about 2%.

Before the open, Deutsche Bank named Palo Alto one of three standouts, along with Snowflake and CrowdStrike, among companies set to gain from rising AI token usage. The bank's reasoning is that expanding data flows, digital identities and attack surfaces support demand for cybersecurity.

And that call landed on a sector that was already rallying.

AI is finding the holes

On Wednesday, the PHP Foundation disclosed two critical flaws in PHP, the programming language behind nearly 70% of websites, and issued an emergency patch. Researchers found the bugs partly with an OpenAI model.

Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora went on the TBPN podcast Wednesday afternoon with a warning: "We're gonna see more of these, not less."

He said Palo Alto's own scan found 22 million places where the PHP flaw persists. He added that whatever today's AI models miss "will definitely be found three months from now with the next model."

Which, yikes.

Why Is Zscaler Stock Going Up?

Shares of Zscaler (ZS) rose 7.8% on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, outpacing a 0.6% gain for the S&P 500. Benzinga reported that shares climbed that day after DA Davidson began covering Zscaler with a Neutral rating and a $215 price target. The stock had closed about where that target sat the day before, only to finish Wednesday about 8% above it. So what are buyers getting from Zscaler's business at the higher price?

Buyers Pay A Premium For Zscaler's Growth

At the October 21 close, Zscaler stock traded at 11.2 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared with 3.1 times for the S&P 500. The stock was far cheaper on that measure at the end of June. At that time, shares traded at 6.8 times the same sales, marking the lowest multiple at any quarter end since fiscal 2018.

That price pays for growth. Zscaler increased its revenue by 25.4% to $3.35 billion in fiscal 2026, the twelve months to July 31, 2026. Management said on its September 3, 2026, earnings call that the results reflected increasing adoption of its Zero Trust platform. Buyers are not paying for a profit yet, however. Zscaler reported a net loss for fiscal 2026, so its price-to-earnings ratio is not meaningful.

Moves like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

Zscaler Is Close To Breaking Even

Zscaler's loss is now small. The company posted an operating loss equal to 0.4% of revenue in fiscal Q4 2026, the three months to July 31. That is down from 4.3% in the same quarter a year earlier. For the full fiscal year, the operating loss settled at 3.6% of revenue, the smallest twelve-month loss relative to revenue at any quarter end since fiscal 2018.

The business also brings in cash alongside that reported loss. Zscaler generated $779 million in free cash flow for fiscal 2026, or 23.2% of revenue. That figure represents the cash left over after spending on equipment and on software Zscaler builds for its own use. Management expects capital spending to stay elevated in fiscal 2027 because components, especially memory, cost more.

Zscaler Expects Slower Growth In Fiscal 2027

The growth buyers are paying for is set to slow, according to management's own forecast. On the September 3 call, executives guided for fiscal 2027 revenue of $3.908 billion to $3.938 billion, representing growth of 16.6% to 17.5%. That pace is slower than the 25% Zscaler reported for fiscal 2026. Furthermore, part of that 25% came from buying Red Canary: without it, revenue grew 20%.

Rapid7, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Okta, and JFrog shares skyrocket, what you need to know
What happened?

A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after sentiment across the broader software and cybersecurity space continued to improve amid receding fears of artificial intelligence disruption.

As detailed by CNBC, investors are continuing to reallocate capital away from semiconductor companies and into software equities amid growing market caution regarding the sustainability of massive infrastructure capital spending and elevated debt financing costs for hardware builders.

This structural dynamic strongly favored cash-generative application and security platforms, which Yahoo Finance noted are positioned to capture incremental corporate spending as enterprises operationalize generative AI at scale.

Serving as a major catalyst for the cybersecurity sector, the NVIDIA Newsroom announced that the chipmaker unveiled its OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin to secure enterprise artificial intelligence agents. The NVIDIA Newsroom detailed that this new architecture establishes standardized frameworks to protect autonomous AI agents, which are software systems capable of executing complex business tasks independently.

Because the deployment of these autonomous agents significantly expands the potential attack surface across enterprise networks, Yahoo Finance explained that security leaders CrowdStrike, Okta, and Zscaler quickly announced they are incorporating OpenShell support to address these new vulnerabilities. Detailing the technical integrations, Yahoo Finance reported that CrowdStrike is plugging its Falcon AI platform directly into the OpenShell runtime to stop rogue agents within milliseconds at the silicon level. Providing the vital identity layer, Okta announced via a joint press release that it will deliver cross-agent authentication controls to ensure AI agents operate with the same least-privilege authorization applied to human workers.

Ultimately, the parallel commitments from cloud-security leaders like Zscaler underscore how deeply integrated zero-trust network access has become as enterprises safely scale their next-generation AI deployments.

Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock rose 6% and Datadog rose 7% today after PHP patched two critical flaws in software that runs an estimated 70% of websites.

Cloudflare gave every customer firewall rules against the known attacks, including free users, which shows why its place in front of millions of sites is valuable.

Analysts expect Cloudflare's revenue to more than double, from $2.17 billion in 2025 to $4.73 billion in 2028.

The stock was already richly valued after a big run this year, so watch whether CISA lists the flaw and whether free users move to paid plans.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) stock jumped 6% today after PHP rushed out emergency patches for two critical flaws in the software behind an estimated 70% of the world's websites. Other stocks tied to protecting websites and apps rose too, including Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ), up 7%.

What exactly happened

The flaws let an attacker take over any web server running PHP 5.4 or later. One of them can also leak passwords, session tokens and API keys. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont called it "one of the biggest vulns in years."

Attackers didn't wait for the fix. Cloudflare logged the first attacks at 3:43 a.m. ET, hours before the official patch landed around 10 a.m. ET.

Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht's response:

"PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free."

The free tier earns its keep

That last line is the story. Cloudflare sits in front of millions of PHP sites, so one set of rules covered all of them at once, before most of their owners could patch.

That's why it pays to give protection away. Every free site Cloudflare shields in a crisis like this one gives its owner a reason to stay, and eventually to pay.

And the paid business is growing fast. Analysts expect revenue to more than double, from $2.17 billion in 2025 to $4.73 billion in 2028…

Nothing in today's news should move those estimates yet. That would take site owners signing up for paid plans after the scare, and the next few quarters will show whether they do.

A big day at a steep price

Today's pop comes right after Cloudflare dropped 15% in a week. Before that, a run had the stock up 78% since January by early October. Before today's move it already traded at nearly 200x forward earnings, and today's jump pushes that higher.

title: AI uncovers massive flaw in web's foundational code
detail:
AI uncovers massive flaw in web's foundational code
Sam Sabin
Wed, October 21, 2026 at 2:26 PM MST 3 min read
NET
Trade NET on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

Security officials are sounding the alarm over two critical vulnerabilities in a programming language used to run millions of websites, marking one of the most consequential cybersecurity discoveries yet made with AI.

Why it matters: The bugs, which researchers found partly with an OpenAI model, proves AI can uncover critical flaws humans missed for decades — raising the stakes for defenders racing to fix vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them at machine speed.

What they're saying: Matthew Prince, the CEO of Cloudflare, a global connectivity and internet security company, said the company saw thousands of attempts to exploit the flaws in the 10 hours before it was publicly announced.

"That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now," he wrote on X.

Driving the news: There are two problems hackers could easily exploit in an open-source programming language known as PHP that's used on nearly 70% of all websites.

Government officials from the U.S. to Japan are warning companies to apply a patch to fix the bugs, or consider taking down their sites to avoid an attack.

OpenAI touted the role its model played in discovering one of the vulnerabilities, which allowed PHP researchers to create a fix.

Between the lines: Security researchers have been skeptical of AI-generated vulnerability reports, many of which have turned out to be minor bugs or false alarms.

But the PHP discovery could force the cybersecurity community to reckon with the reality of AI threats.

"It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits," OpenAI said in a blog post Wednesday.

Threat level: If exploited, the PHP flaws would allow malicious hackers to take control of vulnerable web servers without needing a password or other credentials.

Since PHP runs under a wide variety of internet applications, that access could allow hackers to take over websites, steal sensitive information and tamper with a website.

Some website owners took their sites down earlier Wednesday, including certain services at Wikipedia and 4chan, until they had time to patch their systems.

"These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history," researchers at Wiz wrote in a post.

The big picture: AI-driven bug discoveries are shining a light on the fragility of the modern internet, which is heavily reliant on a slew of open-source software powered by volunteers.
